papers.title: Modulations of the photoswitching performances of azobenzene-based molecular devices by the {\pi}-conjugated spacers
papers.abstract: The nature of the {\pi}-conjugated spacer is a key element to tune the electrical conductance and optical switching properties of metal-spacer-azobenzene-metal molecular devices. We report that the azobenzene-based molecular junctions with a thiophene or a phenylthiophene spacer exhibit a high cis/trans conductance ratio (ca. 1,000), while those with a bithiophene spacer have a lower conductance switching ratio (ca. 500) at the stated conditions (light wavelength and intensity) and for one batch of samples (out of two). Similarly, the two former molecular junctions have quite similar trans-to-cis isomerization kinetics, while the latter has a lower switching rate. The energy level of the highest occupied molecular orbital, which controls the electron transfer in the molecular junction, is weakly influenced by the nature of the spacer, nor by the conformation of the azobenzene moieties. The large increase in the conductance of the molecular junction with azobenzene in the cis-state is explained by an increase in the electronic coupling energy between the molecule and the top electrode. Theoretical studies by Density Functional Theory and Non Equilibrium Green's Functions are qualitatively consistent with the experiments. We find a consistent structure-property trend, showing that the higher molecule/electrode coupling energy for the cis-state is explained by the top benzene ring of the azobenzene lying flat with respect to the top electrode for the thiophene, phenylthiophene and bithiophene spacers. On the contrary, we observe that a spacer with a carbon-carbon triple bond (acetylene thiophene) induces a large irreproducibility and unpredictability of the results.

papers.title: Emission regimes and characteristic energy scales in reverse-biased 4H-SiC Schottky barriers: unified field-emission formulas and energy-dependent tunneling effective mass
papers.abstract: Reverse leakage in 4H-SiC Schottky barrier diodes is analyzed using a current integral with Fermi-Dirac supply and WKB transmission. The ratio of the interface field to a critical field $F_c$ sets the depth of the thermionic-field-emission (TFE) saddle point. The Airy energy distinguishes the thermionic-tunneling crossover, the validity of the TFE formula, and the TFE/field-emission (FE) boundary, which generalizes to $c_1 k_B T \approx 1$ for arbitrary barrier shapes. Closed-form FE and TFE expressions are given for triangular and quadratic barriers; for the latter, the Padovani-Stratton formulas give 1.4-7.9 times (FE, $10^{19}$ cm$^{-3}$) and 2.5-3.6 times (TFE, low-doped layers, 300-433 K) the WKB current, whereas the present expressions agree within 15% and 2%. Applied to Ti/4H-SiC data (30-160 {\deg}C, 50-950 V), an energy-dependent tunneling mass from the complex band structure reduces the residual from 0.17 to 0.11-0.12 dex; it can be implemented in device simulation via the Franz two-band dispersion.

papers.title: Ultra-Wideband Stacked Patch Antenna for D-Band Applications
papers.abstract: This article proposes a wideband stacked dual-patch antenna designed for D-band applications. The antenna is demonstrated with both wireless and dielectric waveguide (DWG) channels. The patch dimensions and spacings are chosen to ensure that the $10~dB$ return loss (RL) bandwidth covers the entire D-band ($110$--$170~GHz$). The antenna is fabricated on a seven-layer organic packaging technology. The patches are fabricated on layers 1 and 3 within a shielding cavity formed by closely spaced vias of $< \lambda/20$ pitch. The fabrication technology supports direct chip-level excitation of the antenna using a flip-chip packaging interface, and the design methodology for this feeding approach is outlined in the paper. In the fabricated design, however, a transition to the WR6 metallic waveguide with ($<~1~dB$) insertion loss (IL) is incorporated for feeding. This facilitates alignment and measurement of the structure using external test equipment. The full antenna and transition are integrated in a back-to-back configuration, achieving a measured $10~dB$ return loss bandwidth of more than $60~GHz$ ($110$--$170~GHz$) for the wireless link, thereby covering the entire D-band. To the best of our knowledge, this is the widest antenna bandwidth reported in the same frequency range. The measured peak gain is $8.5~dBi$ (35$^\circ$ H-plane $3~dB$ beamwidth) with a gain variation of $3.5~dBi$ within the operating bandwidth. For the dielectric waveguide configuration, the measured $10~dB$ RL bandwidth also exceeds $60~GHz$, fully encompassing the D-band. The simulated insertion loss coupling into the dielectric waveguide is $3.5~dB$. A 1-meter dielectric waveguide channel fed with the proposed antenna is measured. The overall channel exhibits a total insertion loss of $14.7~dB$, of which a simulated $3.5~dB$ at $140~GHz$ is attributed to the loss of each side that feeds the DWG.

papers.title: Compact Slow-Wave Hybrid Magnonics on Ultrahigh-Permittivity Substrates
papers.abstract: Hybrid magnonics based on spoof surface plasmon polaritons (SSPPs) enables strong, broadband magnon-photon coupling, but the centimeter-scale device footprints required at low gigahertz frequencies hinder integration. Here, we demonstrate miniaturized slow-wave hybrid magnonic devices using an ultrahigh-permittivity ceramic substrate ($\varepsilon = 140$). Owing to the inverse-square-root dependence of the SSPP plasma frequency on effective permittivity, the required corrugation finger length is reduced by nearly a factor of four compared with conventional microwave substrates. The ceramic is thick and brittle, and conventional thin-film processes cannot easily pattern thick, low-loss conductors on it. We overcome this challenge with additively manufactured electronics (AME). In a customized AME workflow, a multi-material inkjet printer first prints a dielectric fixture that holds and registers the ceramic. After the ceramic is loaded, the printer prints thick silver SSPP patterns directly onto it. Measurements on six printed devices with different finger lengths confirm the predicted geometry-frequency scaling. Moreover, the enhanced field confinement of the compact SSPP waveguide nearly doubles the magnon-photon coupling strength and yields ultrastrong coupling with $g/f_\mathrm{p} \approx 22\%$. Notably, this performance is achieved using a YIG film whose magnetic volume is more than an order of magnitude smaller than that employed in previous SSPP demonstrations. These results establish AME on ultrahigh-permittivity substrates as a practical route toward compact, strongly coupled hybrid magnonic devices.

papers.title: N-Polar AlGaN/GaN Heterojunction Bipolar Transistor
papers.abstract: Heterojunction bipolar transistors based on the III-Nitride systems have significantly lower performance than field effect transistors due to challenges associated with p-type doping of the base. N-polar AlGaN/GaN HBTs can overcome these challenges by polarization-induced holes in the base and base-emitter interface. We experimentally demonstrate the first N-polar AlGaN/GaN heterojunction bipolar transistors (HBTs) grown by plasma-assisted molecular beam epitaxy on GaN substrate without emitter regrowth. The HBTs exhibit a peak current gain of approximately 15, peak differential current gain of approximately 18, and emitter-area-normalized peak current densities exceeding 20 kA/cm^2 and 66 kA/cm^2 for emitter areas of 10 x 10 um^2 and 3 x 10 um^2, respectively. The specific contact resistance for base is estimated 1.32 x 10^{-2} Ohm.cm^2. The open-base breakdown voltage is characterized ~63 V for a 300 nm collector without dielectric passivation. This work lays the foundation for future development of N-polar III-Nitride HBTs for next-generation RF applications.

papers.title: Witnessing Gaussian Coexistence and Correlation-Ellipse Tomography
papers.abstract: Gaussian light is specified by second-order field moments, yet their hidden correlation geometry can demand higher-order intensity measurements. We establish a measurement hierarchy for "Gaussian coexistence", i.e., the simultaneous presence of cross covariance and cross pseudocovariance. For two zero-mean Gaussian modes with circular marginals, all unperturbed intensity moments of second or third order are blind to coexistence. In contrast, a balanced fourth-order residual provides a necessary and sufficient witness. Their identities, however, remain fundamentally ambiguous: recovering the two correlation strengths does not reveal which belongs to the covariance and which to the pseudocovariance. Unexpectedly, adding thermal fluctuations resolves this ambiguity: an independent, correlated thermal probe selectively modifies the covariance while leaving the pseudocovariance unchanged, allowing the two correlation strengths to be individually identified. Moreover, a coherent reference in only one arm then makes their relative phase accessible through third-order intensity correlation. Together, these measurements reconstruct a correlation ellipse and its Poincar\'e-sphere coordinates, determining the relative channel strengths and the ellipse orientation. The framework separates what intensity detection can witness, what thermal probing can identify, and what a single phase reference can orient, turning inaccessible Gaussian correlation structure into a quantitatively reconstructible geometry.

papers.title: Simulation of S-parameters of general multilayer boxed PCBs with the method of moments and the scattering matrix algorithm
papers.abstract: This paper addresses the problem of modeling high-frequency parameters for shielded printed circuit boards (PCBs) using the Green's function for a multilayer waveguide and the S-matrix formalism. The proposed approach incorporates a simple, intuitive method for calculating the full tensor Green's function. The corresponding matrix elements are described using three sets of S-matrices associated with the dielectric layers of the PCB substrate. The method of moments (MoM) is implemented using surface "roof-top" functions, as well as volumetric pulse and linear basis functions; all overlap integrals involving these functions and the waveguide modes are derived in explicit form, enabling the efficient modeling of both planar metallization layers and vertical interconnects. To accelerate computations, a new approach to deriving the expansion of the MoM matrix elements is proposed, which facilitates the application of the fast Fourier transform.

papers.title: Ancilla-assisted multi-qubit quantum gates with polar molecules
papers.abstract: Quantum error correction enables reliable quantum computation using imperfect physical gates, but its implementation often requires multi-qubit controlled-unitary gates $\text{C}_{\mathbb{N}}(U)$ acting on $\mathbb{N} \ge 3$ qubits. Their direct realization is challenging, while decomposing them into standard one-qubit and two-qubit gates can increase circuit depth and error rates. Here, we present an ancilla-assisted scheme to directly implement $\text{C}_{\mathbb{N}}(U)$ in optically trapped ultracold polar molecules. By appropriately selecting qubit states for the ancilla and data qubits, dark states can appear during two smooth $\pi$ pulses. This can generate a controlled-phase gate with the phase set by the relative phase between the pulses; notably, a single $2\pi$ pulse yields a $\text{C}_{\mathbb{N}}(Z)$ gate. Numerical analysis for a simple molecular spatial configuration demonstrates that the gate infidelity is dominated by qubit decoherence, yielding a $\text{C}_2(Z)$ fidelity of $0.996$ estimated with $T_2^\ast=1.5$~s and a gate duration of $T \approx 4\text{~ms}$. Furthermore, diabatic errors remain low, on the order of $10^{-4}$ for $\mathbb{N}=2,3$ and $10^{-3}$ for $\mathbb{N}=4$, even with dipole-dipole interaction strengths as low as $25\hbar/T$.

papers.title: Breaking the Sensitivity Barrier in Fiber-Coupled Terahertz Spectroscopy
papers.abstract: Fiber-coupled terahertz time-domain spectroscopy (THz-TDS) offers the flexibility and robustness needed for practical applications beyond controlled laboratory environments, but its sensitivity has remained substantially below that of free-space systems. Overcoming this limitation requires simultaneously achieving high-efficiency terahertz generation and detection, high-power femtosecond optical pulse delivery, and resilience to optical polarization fluctuations. Here, we demonstrate a fiber-coupled THz-TDS architecture that breaks this sensitivity barrier by integrating polarization-resilient plasmonic nanoantenna arrays with hollow-core antiresonant fibers. We establish a design principle that overcomes the intrinsic polarization sensitivity of plasmonic optoelectronic devices by exploiting the interplay between polarization-dependent optical absorption, ultrafast photocarrier transport, and local electric-field distributions. Through theoretical modeling and experimental validation, we show that engineering this interplay enables highly efficient terahertz generation and detection across different optical polarization states without compromising plasmonically enhanced optoelectronic efficiency. By suppressing optical dispersion and nonlinearities during high-power femtosecond pulse delivery, hollow-core antiresonant fibers further enable the superior optoelectronic properties of GaAs-based photoconductors to be fully exploited while preserving the flexibility and robustness of fiber coupling. The resulting system generates record-high terahertz radiation powers and achieves a 145-dB peak dynamic range in 60 seconds, representing a 300-fold improvement over state-of-the-art fiber-coupled THz-TDS systems.

papers.title: Micrometer-sized magnonic three-port rectilinear circulator
papers.abstract: The development of miniaturized non-reciprocal microwave technologies compatible with integrated circuit architectures remains a critical challenge for modern information technology. Here, we present the first experimental characterization of a micron-sized prototypical magnon circulator. Taking advantage of the chiral excitation of spin-waves via nanowire gratings, we propose an original design of a circulator involving three channels of rectilinear and unidirectional spin-wave beams. We demonstrate via a full 3-port spin-wave spectroscopy a genuine spin-wave circulation between the three ports. The narrow frequency band of operation can be tuned over a broad range of frequencies (2-8 GHz) with both an external field of up to 100 mT, and the dimensions of the grating specifying the wavevectors. This proposed scheme opens up possibilities for architectures of integrated and miniaturized non-reciprocal microwave devices.

papers.title: Microphase Separation and Ionic Aggregation in Oppositely Charged End-Functionalized Polymer Blends
papers.abstract: Using an ion-correlation-augmented self-consistent field theory (IC-SCFT), we study the phase behavior of binary blends of A and B polymers carrying single end groups of opposite charge. Under the low dielectric conditions typical for organic polymer melts, strong ion correlations drive association of multiple chain ends, leading to emergent multichain architectures that go beyond a simple ion-paired diblock copolymer picture previously used to interpret recent experiments. At moderate to strong polymer segregation, the resulting phase diagram differs considerably from this effective-diblock prediction: ion clustering broadens the lamellar and cylindrical windows while suppressing the network phases, the reverse of the trend for end-charged diblock copolymers. At weak segregation, the two polymers remain miscible even as ion clustering persists, and decreasing chain length drives the clusters themselves through a sphere-to-cylinder-to-lamella shape transition, connecting continuously to the aggregation behavior of classical terminally charged ionomers in the limit when one of the polymer species shrinks to just the charged end. These results reveal that ion clustering - beyond simple pairwise bonding - shapes the self-assembly of end-charged polymer blends.

papers.title: Galvanometer Mirror Based Femtosecond-Laser Volumetric Displays
papers.abstract: Femtosecond-laser-induced plasma enables self-emissive voxels to be generated directly in air for drawing three-dimensional images. Galvanometer-mirror-based beam scanning provides a method for rapidly moving plasma voxels using a relatively simple optical configuration. However, the generated plasma voxels are not ideal points but luminous regions with finite lengths and widths. Variations in voxel shape and orientation caused by focusing and scanning conditions may therefore affect the appearance of rendered points and lines. Nevertheless, quantitative relationships between focusing and scanning conditions and plasma-voxel geometry remain insufficiently characterized in systems using a two-axis galvanometer mirror and a single focusing lens. Here, we quantitatively investigate how focal length and two-axis galvanometer scan angle affect the shape of plasma voxels and the projected inclination of their principal axes. For focal lengths ranging from 75 to 300 mm, the mean plasma length increased from 1.39 to 4.64 mm. These results indicate that increasing the focal length produces more elongated and anisotropic plasma voxels. The projected inclination of the plasma principal axis varied approximately linearly with the corresponding scan angle, although the response differed between the two scanning axes. These results provide quantitative design data for selecting focusing conditions and correcting voxel shape and orientation according to scanning conditions in galvanometer-mirror-based aerial volumetric displays.
